baseline.note: Historical runtime evidence (2026-10-24..2026-10-31) was produced by an older build (HEAD ~71a952b/2cea664) and must not be assumed to describe current HEAD d987c7f. Runtime evidence is context; executable code and tests are authoritative.

decisions.title: Signal validity window and delayed/ambiguous entry submission
decisions.historical_evidence: One place_order call took ~921s with a 5s CLI timeout. Claim-to-submit delays of 34 and 65 minutes were observed. Two intents passed through unknown_requires_reconciliation and later resolved.
decisions.decision: Signal validity is configurable from Telegram (default 12h) and is distinct from accepted-order lifetime. Entry submission may be retried only while the signal is valid. After expiry no new order is submitted for that signal, but an already accepted open order is never cancelled by expiry. Ambiguous submissions persist as UNKNOWN, survive restart, and are reconciled against MEXC before any further submission. Never resend after a timeout.
required_behavior: signals older than the configured validity window are rejected before intent creation
a persisted intent deadline is enforced before every submission attempt and after restart
signal expiry never cancels an accepted open order
ambiguous submit outcomes persist as unknown_requires_reconciliation and are never auto-retried
the CLI write timeout bounds the whole call, not only the child process
acceptance_criteria: expired signal is rejected with signal_expired and no order is sent
an accepted open order survives signal expiry
unknown intent is never resubmitted automatically and is reconciled read-only
CLI write that exceeds timeout_s raises an uncertain error and returns control to the caller
decisions.limitations: Deadline is evaluated against the persisted signal deadline; clock skew between host and Telegram is not modelled.

decisions.title: Centralized MEXC API rate limiting
decisions.historical_evidence: 192,994 operations / 57h (~0.92 ops/s). Estimated 70 weight/10s for one symbol and 110 for three against an internal cap of 60. No HTTP 429 observed.
decisions.decision: One simple centralized weighted limiter covers every MEXC request. Endpoint weights are applied, a configurable safety margin is kept, non-essential requests are briefly deferred near the cap, server retry timing is honoured on 429, and weight/wait/error data is recorded. No multi-tier queues, emergency capacity, adaptive schedulers or priority infrastructure. The historical 60 was an internal cap, not a proven exchange hard limit.
required_behavior: every REST call passes through the shared weighted gate before being sent
gate wait time is measured, logged on contention, and persisted on recorded operations
per-10s caps remain configurable with validated bounds
429/Retry-After is honoured and never retried blindly
acceptance_criteria: gate returns the wait duration and exposes aggregate statistics
an operation that waited records rate_limit_wait_ms > 0
caps can be lowered/raised via config within validation bounds
decisions.limitations: Exchange-side hard limits are not measured; caps remain a local safety margin.

decisions.title: MEXC WebSocket market data
decisions.historical_evidence: 9,798 disconnects, zero successful connections, invalid frame/mask and Pong handling.
decisions.decision: REST remains the market-data mechanism. WebSocket is not repaired or migrated now and no WebSocket complexity is added. Reconsider only if a demonstrated need appears.
required_behavior: market data keeps using REST polling
no new WebSocket dependency or repair work is introduced
failed WebSocket attempts never block trading or monitoring
acceptance_criteria: polling feed delivers prices used by the monitor
no blocking call is made on the Telegram event loop for market data
tests_required: existing market-data tests continue to pass
decisions.limitations: WebSocket feed remains non-functional by design decision; only polling is used.

decisions.title: Stale price handling in the tick queue
decisions.historical_evidence: 3,324 price events delayed over 60s with a single worker and a 1,000-entry queue that silently dropped the oldest events.
decisions.decision: No separate queue redesign. Periodic MEXC reconciliation reduces practical risk. Simple stale-price safeguards may remain. Freshness must still be checked before any immediate price decision; reconciliation is not a substitute for freshness.
required_behavior: a price observation older than the stale threshold is never used to trigger an entry
tick work stays off the asyncio event loop
periodic reconciliation is the primary safety net for exchange state
acceptance_criteria: stale ticks are rejected before any submission path
no per-tick exchange polling remains in the price path
decisions.limitations: Queue backlog metrics remain unavailable; the queue stays bounded with drop-oldest semantics.

decisions.title: Missed Telegram messages during downtime
decisions.historical_evidence: Messages 19392-19446 were missed during a 10h33m outage.
decisions.decision: No historical backfill. On startup a fresh processing boundary is established and only signals published after the bot started monitoring are processed. Older messages are ignored even inside the validity window and are never replayed.
required_behavior: per-channel forward-only activation boundary is persisted at startup
messages at or below the boundary never produce an intent
backfill/recovery sources never trade
acceptance_criteria: boundary is written before handlers register
a message at/below the boundary is stored/audited and never traded
decisions.limitations: Messages posted during downtime remain absent from the archive (by decision).

decisions.title: Same-symbol duplicate BUY protection
decisions.historical_evidence: has_active_trade_for_symbol / has_active_intent_for_symbol were unused. Five same-symbol overlaps: APE x1, ICP x3, LPT x1.
decisions.decision: Do not block a new signal merely because a prior same-symbol trade is open. Before every BUY, verify MEXC has no open order for that symbol, using a fresh reconciliation snapshot when available and a direct query otherwise. Unverifiable state blocks the entry. No artificial per-symbol trade-count limits.
required_behavior: every BUY passes the exchange open-order check for its symbol
a failed/unavailable check fails closed for that symbol only
dead per-symbol guard functions are removed rather than left misleading
acceptance_criteria: BUY rejected when MEXC reports an open order for the symbol
BUY allowed on unrelated symbols while another symbol is open
decisions.limitations: A held position with no open orders is intentionally not blocked (matches decision).

decisions.title: BUY Block enforcement
decisions.historical_evidence: new_buys_blocked was diagnostic-only; SubmissionGate never enforced it while notifications claimed BUYs were blocked.
decisions.decision: The existing Telegram BUY Block must actually prevent all new entry BUY submissions. Existing positions and their TP/SL/OCO management continue. Enabling it never cancels or modifies existing orders. Telegram status must reflect the enforced state.
required_behavior: entry submissions are refused while the persisted BUY block is active
protection submissions (OCO/cancel) are unaffected
status/readiness text states the block is enforced
acceptance_criteria: entry submission raises SubmissionBlocked with the block reason
OCO protection still succeeds while the block is active
decisions.limitations: None identified.

decisions.title: SQLite concurrency correctness
decisions.historical_evidence: check_same_thread=False, reads outside the shared lock, WAL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, 10s busy timeout, no observed lock errors.
decisions.decision: Keep SQLite. Critical trading state changes stay atomic; lock contention is logged; bounded retries are used where appropriate. No replacement or new concurrency infrastructure.
required_behavior: write transactions are atomic and serialized
lock contention is retried a bounded number of times and logged
no partially updated order/trade state is observable
acceptance_criteria: a locked database retries then raises a clear error
contention produces a log line with the operation
decisions.limitations: Reads still use the shared connection; no per-thread connections were introduced.

decisions.title: Minimum order notional
decisions.historical_evidence: OCO legs around 1.5 USDT; no confirmed minimum-notional rejects.
decisions.decision: Not a priority. No complex subsystem without evidence. Existing symbol validation is kept.
required_behavior: existing symbol filter validation remains active before submission
acceptance_criteria: symbol validation failures remain fail-closed
tests_required: existing symbol validation tests continue to pass
decisions.limitations: Exchange filters are not cached locally; exact per-symbol minimums require a live read.

decisions.title: Existing protective controls
decisions.historical_evidence: max_ip_weight / max_uid_weight existed only in code; require_control_setup and _dimension_ok were unused in expected paths.
decisions.decision: No new control features. Ensure existing controls work, only the designated owner account executes administrative commands, BUY Block is enforced, Telegram status matches reality, and misleading no-op controls are removed. No new roles, emergency stop or approval workflow.
required_behavior: owner-only administrative commands are enforced by numeric user id
status output matches enforced behaviour
dead control parameters are removed rather than silently ignored
acceptance_criteria: developer role cannot execute owner commands
no unused readiness/control parameter remains in the submission gate
decisions.limitations: No second-owner/admin expansion is introduced.

decisions.title: Standalone TP order path
decisions.historical_evidence: _enter_tp1 -> _submit_tp_order remained reachable while OCO exits existed.
decisions.decision: Exit management uses native OCO orders only. Obsolete standalone TP submission paths are removed or disabled and never silently used as a fallback.
required_behavior: no code path submits a standalone TP limit order
exits are submitted as OCO pairs only
acceptance_criteria: standalone TP helpers raise or are removed
only OCO submission remains reachable
decisions.limitations: Legacy rows in old databases are left untouched.

decisions.title: OCO retry policy and per-attempt reporting
decisions.historical_evidence: Three attempts instead of the agreed schedule; attempt-level notification tracking insufficient; uniqueness key suppressed repeats.
decisions.decision: One initial OCO attempt plus eight retries with delays 5,10,15,30,30,30,30,30 seconds. Definitive validation errors are not retried. Ambiguous outcomes are persisted UNKNOWN and reconciled, never blindly replaced. State survives restarts. No automatic Market Sell after exhaustion. No automatic price changes. Each important attempt and outcome is traceable and notified to both recipients.
required_behavior: retry schedule is persisted per leg and honoured across restarts
definitive rejections are terminal for that leg
each attempt produces its own durable notification row per recipient
exhaustion produces a critical unprotected notification
acceptance_criteria: attempt counter and next-attempt time are persisted
ninth failure stops retrying
two recipients each have one row per attempt
decisions.limitations: Retries are driven by the periodic reconciliation worker.

decisions.title: Excessive per-tick OCO leg polling
decisions.historical_evidence: Two PENDLE OCO legs polled every ~2s for ~53h; ~57,339 checks per leg.
decisions.decision: Use the shared periodic MEXC reconciliation process for open orders, fills, OCO groups, child legs and local trade states. MEXC is the source of truth when available. Record and notify discrepancies. Block dependent actions while critical discrepancies remain. No separate OCO reconciliation subsystem. The interval is validated against endpoint weights before being fixed.
required_behavior: no exchange order queries from the price-tick path
open orders/legs are reconciled by the periodic worker
interval is derived from measured weight budget
acceptance_criteria: tick handling performs no REST order query
reconciliation interval produces a documented weight estimate
decisions.limitations: Reconciliation latency is bounded by the configured interval.

decisions.title: Partial entry fill protection
decisions.historical_evidence: No real partial entry fill observed; protection was only placed after the intent became terminal.
decisions.decision: Protect acquired quantity immediately even while the entry order is still open, in proportion to the filled amount. Keep the unfilled remainder working. If SL closes the acquired position, cancel the unfilled remainder so it cannot create an unwanted position. If TP1 executes, cancel the unfilled remainder. Manage the remaining position to TP2/SL. Validate against MEXC capabilities without real orders.
required_behavior: OCO protection is submitted as soon as a non-zero fill is confirmed
protection quantity equals the acquired quantity, split for TP1/TP2
unfilled entry remainder is cancelled when SL or TP1 executes
acceptance_criteria: partial fill produces OCO coverage for the filled quantity
cancelling the remainder never resubmits the entry
decisions.limitations: Exchange-side OCO quantity constraints are respected by the existing symbol validation.

decisions.title: Manual entry cancellation
decisions.historical_evidence: One manual cancellation detected after ~3m41s.
decisions.decision: Periodically read entry-order status. A manual cancellation is accepted, never resubmitted, and notified to both recipients. Any already-filled quantity is protected per the partial-fill rules. Manual sales are not detected or managed.
required_behavior: manual cancel transitions the intent/trade without resubmission
acquired quantity remains protected
both recipients are notified
acceptance_criteria: cancel detected on the next reconciliation produces a notification and no new order
decisions.limitations: Detection latency equals the reconciliation interval.

decisions.title: Manual sales and unknown exchange orders
decisions.historical_evidence: Manual PENDLE/LINK sales undetected; an MYX order existed on the exchange but not in the DB; startup cleanup cancelled a real MYX order because its value was below $5.
decisions.decision: Owner interference is the owner's responsibility; no manual-sale detection subsystem. However, startup cleanup and unknown-order handling must never cancel or modify an order merely because it is missing locally or small. Unknown real orders are never cancelled automatically.
required_behavior: startup cleanup performs no automatic cancellation
unattributed orders are reported and left untouched
only explicitly attributed bot orders may ever be cancelled by bot logic
acceptance_criteria: cleanup run leaves every exchange order in place
report lists unattributed orders
decisions.limitations: Manual sales remain invisible by design decision.

decisions.title: 100-trade monitoring limit
decisions.historical_evidence: list_trades(limit=100) with 20 trades in production.
decisions.decision: 100 is sufficient. No pagination or new subsystem now. Revisit only if usage approaches the limit.
required_behavior: existing limit is retained
acceptance_criteria: no behaviour change
tests_required: existing trade listing tests continue to pass
decisions.limitations: Above 100 trades the oldest non-terminal trades would leave the tick/monitor window.

decisions.title: Telegram notification reliability
decisions.historical_evidence: 313 notifications, none pending/failed at audit end, 21 failed attempts later succeeded, ambiguous outcomes not handled, some global BUY_BLOCK keys allowed only one notification.
decisions.decision: Both configured recipients receive important trading and system notifications. Delivery state is tracked per recipient; success for one never masks failure for the other. Failed deliveries retry in a controlled manner. Ambiguous outcomes are preserved and reported safely. Important attempts are individually traceable. Recipient configuration is verified, not assumed. No credentials in reports.
required_behavior: one durable row per recipient per event
ambiguous delivery is surfaced to recipients, not silently dropped
event keys are scoped so identical events for different trades are not deduplicated
acceptance_criteria: failure for one recipient leaves the other unaffected
an ambiguous delivery produces a visible alert
decisions.limitations: Owner B delivery depends on the configured chat id; absence is reported, never invented.

decisions.title: OCO local database consistency
decisions.historical_evidence: 30/30 oco_group_id NULL; 18 take_profit rows and zero stop_loss rows; MYX local/exchange contradiction; LPT order-id mismatch.
decisions.decision: No separate OCO reconciliation subsystem. Shared periodic reconciliation covers OCO groups, both legs, fills and local state. MEXC is the source of truth when available; otherwise the latest local state is used but explicitly marked unverified/stale, and reconciled again when the exchange is reachable.
required_behavior: both OCO legs (take-profit and stop-loss) are persisted with group attribution
trade orders carry their oco_group_id
fallback state is marked unverified
acceptance_criteria: a submitted OCO yields one group and two legs with attribution
when the exchange is unreachable the leg is marked unverified, not confirmed
decisions.limitations: Historical rows are not rewritten.

decisions.title: Incorrect MEXC error classification
decisions.historical_evidence: "limit price needs to be greater than the latest price" became MexcServerError then UNKNOWN; two cases.
decisions.decision: Definitive validation/rejection errors are classified as rejected with the real reason, not UNKNOWN. Network/timeout ambiguity stays UNKNOWN and is reconciled before any replacement. Both recipients are notified accurately. Prefer a minimal correction over a new error framework.
required_behavior: deterministic exchange validation errors are terminal rejections
ambiguous transport errors remain uncertain
notifications state the real reason
acceptance_criteria: price-relationship rejection maps to a rejection, not uncertainty
timeout still maps to uncertainty
decisions.limitations: Classification is text-based on the CLI envelope; unknown messages keep the conservative uncertain mapping.
